1086	    def import_bundle(
1087	        self, tenant_id: str, payload: dict
1088	    ) -> tuple:
1089	        """Persist a validated export payload under the importing tenant.
1090	
1091	        Returns (IMPORT_CREATED, record) for a brand-new key_id, or
1092	        (IMPORT_CONFLICT, existing) when the key_id already exists; the
1093	        existing record on disk is never touched, and the caller decides 409
1094	        versus 404 from its owner. Every version is adopted through the
1095	        matching provider (a mismatch raises ProviderUnavailable -> 503 and
1096	        malformed material ProviderInvalidMaterial -> 400) **before** the
1097	        conflict recheck or any file is written; handles minted by a refused
1098	        or failed attempt are all deleted and no file or audit line changes.
1099	        A successful import and its audit event commit through the same
1100	        outbox transaction as create/rotate.
1101	        """
1102	        key_id = payload["key_id"]
1103	        # Mint the committing event up front so the provision journal is
1104	        # named after its event_id: a leftover journal resolves at any startup
1105	        # by asking the ledger whether the event committed.
1106	        event = self.audit.new_event(
1107	            tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT, key_id,
1108	            audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
1109	        )
1110	        journal_id, journal_path = self._new_provision_journal(event.event_id)
1111	        try:
1112	            adopted = []  # (provider, handle)
1113	            versions = []
1114	            try:
1115	                for ver in payload["versions"]:
1116	                    version_record, target = self._adopt_imported_version(
1117	                        ver, journal_path
1118	                    )
1119	                    versions.append(version_record)
1120	                    adopted.append((target, version_record.handle))
1121	            except BaseException:
1122	                self._release_handles(adopted)
1123	                raise
1124	            record = KeyRecord(
1125	                key_id=key_id,
1126	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
1127	                label=payload["label"],
1128	                versions=versions,
1129	                current_version=payload["current_version"],
1130	                status=payload["status"],
1131	                reason=payload["reason"],
1132	                operator=payload["operator"],
1133	                revoked_at=payload["revoked_at"],
1134	            )
1135	            path = self._path_for(key_id)
1136	            with self._key_lock(key_id), self._file_lock(key_id):
1137	                # Conflict recheck only after every version validated and
1138	                # every provider call succeeded; nothing has been written.
1139	                existing = self._read_record(path)
1140	                if existing is not None:
1141	                    self._release_handles(adopted)
1142	                    return IMPORT_CONFLICT, existing
1143	                try:
1144	                    # Rollback of the just-created file plus explicit handle
1145	                    # release below; the provision journal also reaps on
1146	                    # crash.
1147	                    self._commit_mutation(
1148	                        path, record, event, None,
1149	                        journal_id=journal_id,
1150	                    )
1151	                except BaseException:
1152	                    self._release_handles(adopted)
1153	                    raise
1154	                # Committed: the handles are owned by the new record and the
1155	                # durable event makes the journal obsolete.
1156	                self.drop_provision_journal(journal_id)
1157	                journal_id = None
1158	            return IMPORT_CREATED, record
1159	        finally:
1160	            if journal_id is not None:
1161	                # Any non-commit exit (provider failure, validation, conflict,
1162	                # aborted transaction): every minted handle was released
1163	                # above; the journal itself is no longer needed.
1164	                self.drop_provision_journal(journal_id)

1277	    @contextmanager
1278	    def multi_key_locks(self, key_ids) -> Iterator[None]:
1279	        """Acquire the per-key locks for many key_ids, in sorted order.
1280	
1281	        A fixed acquisition order keeps this deadlock-free against the
1282	        restore transaction, which also takes its key locks sorted.
1283	        """
1284	        acquired = []
1285	        try:
1286	            for key_id in sorted(set(key_ids)):
1287	                lock_cm = self.key_locks(key_id)
1288	                lock_cm.__enter__()
1289	                acquired.append(lock_cm)
1290	            yield
1291	        finally:
1292	            for lock_cm in reversed(acquired):
1293	                lock_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)

1	"""Atomic tenant restore: multi-file outbox transaction over keys and policy.
2	
3	A restore writes several key files and optionally one policy document as a
4	single logical transaction. Every file first lands carrying the same pending
5	marker (the shared audit event plus a manifest of the whole write set); the
6	single audit event is appended to the ledger once; only then are the markers
7	cleared. A failure or crash at any point is repaired idempotently on the next
8	open, mirroring the per-key outbox in :mod:`keymgr.store` and the policy
9	outbox in :mod:`keymgr.policy`.
10	
11	Conflict rules, applied before anything touches disk:
12	
13	* a ``key_id`` that already exists for the requesting tenant is a ``409``
14	  (nothing is changed);
15	* a ``key_id`` owned by another tenant answers ``404`` so existence never
16	  leaks across tenants;
17	* a policy document already present for the tenant conflicts regardless of
18	  whether the bundle carries rules or an explicit null (an existing policy is
19	  never overwritten or deleted); a document on the tenant's hashed path that
20	  names another owner is treated as a foreign ``404``.
21	
22	An empty bundle (``keys == []`` and ``policy is null``) creates no files but
23	still commits the single ``import`` event and reports success.
24	"""
25	
26	import hashlib
27	import json
28	import os
29	import threading
30	from contextlib import contextmanager
31	from typing import Dict, Iterator, List, NamedTuple, Optional
32	
33	from . import audit as audit_mod
34	from . import tenantbundle
35	from .audit import AuditEvent, LedgerError
36	from .policy import Rule

38	try:  # fcntl is POSIX-only; restores still work without cross-process locks.
39	    import fcntl
40	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
41	    fcntl = None
42	
43	# Restore outcomes.
44	RESTORE_CREATED = "created"
45	RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT = "same_tenant_conflict"
46	RESTORE_FOREIGN_CONFLICT = "foreign_conflict"
47	
48	# An empty restore writes no key/policy file, so it persists its idempotency
49	# marker as ``restore-empty-<sha256(tenant_id)>.json`` in the data directory:
50	# the batch commits at most once and a repeated empty restore of the same
51	# tenant conflicts instead of logging a second import event.
52	_EMPTY_MARKER_PREFIX = "restore-empty-"

54	
55	class Conflict(NamedTuple):
56	    """Why a restore was refused before writing anything."""

58	    kind: str  # "key" or "policy"
59	    owner: Optional[str]  # tenant that currently owns the object
60	    key_id: Optional[str] = None  # set for kind == "key"

63	class RestoreResult(NamedTuple):
64	    """Outcome of a restore attempt."""

66	    status: str
67	    tenant_id: Optional[str] = None
68	    key_ids: Optional[List[str]] = None

73	class _PendingGroup:
74	    """Files sharing one restore marker discovered during recovery."""
75	
76	    def __init__(self, marker: dict) -> None:
77	        self.marker = marker
78	        self.key_files: Dict[str, str] = {}  # key_id -> path
79	        self.policy_file: Optional[str] = None
80	        self.policy_tenant: Optional[str] = None

82	        self.journal: Optional[str] = marker.get("journal")

85	class RestoreCoordinator:
86	    """Coordinates reads for backup and the atomic write set for restore."""

88	    def __init__(self, store, policy_store) -> None:
89	        self.store = store
90	        self.policy_store = policy_store
91	        # Serialize restores within this process; per-key fcntl locks plus the
92	        # policy write lock still guard individual files.
93	        self._restore_lock = threading.Lock()
94	        # Recover any multi-file transaction interrupted by a crash.
95	        self.recover()

97	    # -- backup ------------------------------------------------------------
98	    def backup_payload(self, tenant_id: str) -> dict:
99	        """Build the decrypted tenant payload {format, tenant_id, keys, policy}.
100	
101	        The read runs under the tenant's policy lock and every key lock of
102	        the tenant (all acquired in the same sorted order the restore
103	        transaction uses), so the bundle is one committed view: a concurrent
104	        rotate/revoke/policy update in any process is either fully before or
105	        fully after the snapshot, never mixed into it.
106	        """
107	        key_ids = [r.key_id for r in self.store.list_for_tenant(tenant_id)]
108	        with self.policy_store.tenant_lock(tenant_id), self.store.multi_key_locks(
109	            key_ids
110	        ):
111	            # Re-read under the locks: a record listed above may have been
112	            # rotated or revoked since the unlocked directory scan.
113	            records = []
114	            for key_id in key_ids:
115	                record = self.store.read_raw(key_id)
116	                if record is not None and record.tenant_id == tenant_id:
117	                    records.append(record)
118	            # Lazily take over any raw pre-provider versions here, under the
119	            # same key locks, so the backup is one committed view. This only
120	            # imports/wraps while the local provider is active; with an
121	            # external provider active a legacy version fails 503 and the
122	            # backup is refused without a fallback.
123	            for record in records:
124	                self.store.prepare_backup_record(record)
125	            rules = self.policy_store.get(tenant_id)
126	            return {
127	                "format": tenantbundle.FORMAT,
128	                "tenant_id": tenant_id,
129	                "keys": [self.store.backup_entry(r) for r in records],
130	                "policy": None
131	                if rules is None
132	                else {"rules": [r.to_json() for r in rules]},
133	            }
134	
135	    def backup_bundle(self, tenant_id: str, passphrase: str) -> str:
136	        """Seal the tenant's full state into an opaque backup bundle."""
137	        return tenantbundle.encode_bundle(
138	            self.backup_payload(tenant_id), passphrase
139	        )

142	    @contextmanager
143	    def _cross_process_restore_lock(self) -> Iterator[None]:
144	        """Serialize whole restore transactions across processes.
145	
146	        The in-process ``_restore_lock`` cannot stop a second server or CLI
147	        process from interleaving its conflict scan with this one's writes;
148	        an exclusive ``fcntl`` lock on ``restore.lock`` can.
149	        """
150	        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
151	            yield
152	            return
153	        fd = os.open(
154	            os.path.join(self.store.data_dir, "restore.lock"),
155	            os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT,
156	            0o600,
157	        )
158	        try:
159	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
160	            yield
161	        finally:
162	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
163	            os.close(fd)

165	    def _empty_marker_path(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
166	        digest = hashlib.sha256(tenant_id.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
167	        return os.path.join(
168	            self.store.data_dir, _EMPTY_MARKER_PREFIX + digest + ".json"
169	        )

171	    def restore(self, tenant_id: str, payload: dict) -> RestoreResult:
172	        """Atomically restore a validated tenant payload.
173	
174	        Returns a created result, or a conflict result after leaving every
175	        existing file byte-for-byte untouched. Raises LedgerError when the
176	        transaction cannot be committed; all written files and all handles
177	        minted by the attempt are rolled back.
178	
179	        Ordering: every version is validated and adopted through its provider
180	        first (the durable provision journal records each handle as it is
181	        minted); only then are conflicts rechecked, files written and the
182	        single audit event appended. A failure, refused conflict or crash at
183	        any point before that commit point deletes every handle the attempt
184	        created; the durable event is the point of no return.
185	        """
186	        with self._restore_lock, self._cross_process_restore_lock():
187	            key_ids = sorted(k["key_id"] for k in payload["keys"])
188	            policy_rules = None
189	            if payload["policy"] is not None:
190	                policy_rules = [
191	                    Rule.from_json(r) for r in payload["policy"]["rules"]
192	                ]
193	
194	            # Mint the committing event up front so the provision journal is
195	            # named after its event_id, letting startup recovery decide
196	            # committed-vs-not purely from the ledger.
197	            event = self.store.audit.new_event(
198	                tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT, None,
199	                audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
200	            )
201	            journal_id, journal_path = self.store._new_provision_journal(
202	                event.event_id
203	            )
204	            try:
205	                # Phase 0: complete ALL version validation and provider
206	                # calls before the conflict recheck or any file write.
207	                records = []
208	                try:
209	                    for key_id in key_ids:
210	                        entry = next(
211	                            k for k in payload["keys"] if k["key_id"] == key_id

213	                        records.append(
214	                            self.store.record_from_backup(
215	                                tenant_id, entry, journal_path
216	                            )
217	                        )
218	                except BaseException:
219	                    # A later key/version failed: release the handles the
220	                    # earlier records already minted (record_from_backup
221	                    # released its own record's handles; do the rest here).
222	                    for record in records:
223	                        self.store.release_record_handles(record)
224	                    raise

226	                # Conflict scan only after every provider call succeeded.
227	                # Any foreign owner anywhere wins (404); otherwise a
228	                # same-tenant owner is a 409. Repeated under every lock.
229	                conflict = self._scan_conflicts(tenant_id, key_ids)
230	                if conflict is not None:
231	                    # Nothing was written; release every minted handle.
232	                    for record in records:
233	                        self.store.release_record_handles(record)

235	                        RESTORE_FOREIGN_CONFLICT
236	                        if conflict.owner != tenant_id
237	                        else RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT
238	                    )
239	                    return RestoreResult(status=status, conflict=conflict)

241	                writes_policy = policy_rules is not None

243	                if not key_ids and not writes_policy:

250	                            owner = self.policy_store.owner_of_path(policy_path)
251	                            if owner is not None and owner != tenant_id:
252	                                return RestoreResult(
253	                                    status=RESTORE_FOREIGN_CONFLICT,
254	                                    conflict=Conflict(kind="policy", owner=owner),
255	                                )

257	                                status=RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT,
258	                                conflict=Conflict(kind="policy", owner=tenant_id),

262	                marker = {
263	                    "_restore": True,

267	                    "policy": writes_policy,
268	                    # Ties the marker group to the attempt's handle journal.
269	                    "journal": journal_id,

274	                )

276	                # On a normal return (success, refused conflict or a handled
277	                # rollback) the handles were either committed to the records
278	                # or released; the journal is spent. A hard crash leaves it on
279	                # disk for startup recovery, which is the actual safety net.
280	                self.store.drop_provision_journal(journal_id)

282	    def _commit_empty(self, tenant_id: str, event: AuditEvent) -> RestoreResult:
283	        """Commit an empty restore: idempotency marker + one import event.
284	
285	        The marker file first lands carrying the pending event, the event is
286	        appended, then the marker is finalized with the event cleared. A
287	        ledger failure removes the marker (nothing commits); a crash is
288	        repaired by recovery exactly like a multi-file restore group.
289	        """
290	        path = self._empty_marker_path(tenant_id)
291	        if os.path.exists(path):
292	            # This tenant already committed an empty restore batch.
293	            return RestoreResult(
294	                status=RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT,
295	                conflict=Conflict(kind="batch", owner=tenant_id),
296	            )
297	        marker = {
298	            "_restore": True,
299	            "_empty": True,
300	            "event": event.to_json(),
301	            "tenant_id": tenant_id,
302	            "key_ids": [],
303	            "policy": False,
304	        }
305	        self.store._write_atomic(path, marker)
306	        try:
307	            self.store.audit.append(event)
308	        except BaseException:
309	            try:
310	                os.unlink(path)
311	            except OSError:
312	                pass
313	            raise
314	        finalized = dict(marker)
315	        finalized["event"] = None
316	        self.store._write_atomic(path, finalized)
317	        return RestoreResult(
318	            status=RESTORE_CREATED,
319	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
320	            key_ids=[],
321	            policy_restored=False,
322	        )

324	    def _scan_conflicts(
325	        self, tenant_id: str, key_ids: List[str]
326	    ) -> Optional[Conflict]:
327	        """Return the first conflict (foreign owners take priority).
328	
329	        A policy document already present for the tenant conflicts even when
330	        the bundle's policy slot is null: a restore never overwrites or
331	        deletes an existing policy.
332	        """
333	        same_tenant: Optional[Conflict] = None
334	        for key_id in key_ids:
335	            existing = self.store.read_raw(key_id)
336	            if existing is None:
337	                continue
338	            if existing.tenant_id != tenant_id:
339	                # A foreign key answers 404 immediately and suppresses any
340	                # same-tenant 409, so cross-tenant existence never leaks.
341	                return Conflict(
342	                    kind="key", owner=existing.tenant_id, key_id=key_id
343	                )
344	            if same_tenant is None:
345	                same_tenant = Conflict(
346	                    kind="key", owner=tenant_id, key_id=key_id
347	                )
348	        path = self.policy_store.path_for(tenant_id)
349	        if os.path.exists(path):
350	            owner = self.policy_store.owner_of_path(path)
351	            if owner is not None and owner != tenant_id:
352	                # The tenant's hashed path holds a document naming another
353	                # tenant; treat it like a foreign occupation.
354	                return Conflict(kind="policy", owner=owner)
355	            if same_tenant is None:
356	                same_tenant = Conflict(kind="policy", owner=tenant_id)
357	        return same_tenant

359	    def _commit(
360	        self,
361	        tenant_id: str,
362	        key_ids: List[str],
363	        records: list,
364	        policy_rules: Optional[List[Rule]],
365	        event: AuditEvent,
366	        marker: dict,
367	    ) -> RestoreResult:
368	        """Run the multi-file outbox transaction under all required locks."""
369	        locked = []
370	        policy_cm = self.policy_store.tenant_lock(tenant_id)
371	        policy_taken = False
372	        try:
373	            policy_cm.__enter__()
374	            policy_taken = True
375	            for key_id in key_ids:
376	                lock_cm = self.store.key_locks(key_id)
377	                lock_cm.__enter__()
378	                locked.append(lock_cm)
379	
380	            # Re-scan now that every file lock is held.
381	            conflict = self._scan_conflicts(tenant_id, key_ids)
382	            if conflict is not None:
383	                status = (
384	                    RESTORE_FOREIGN_CONFLICT
385	                    if conflict.owner != tenant_id
386	                    else RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT
387	                )
388	                # The provider objects were minted before the locks, but no
389	                # file now commits: release the handles so the backend leaks
390	                # nothing on the lost conflict race.
391	                for record in records:
392	                    self.store.release_record_handles(record)
393	                return RestoreResult(status=status, conflict=conflict)
394	
395	            written_keys: List[str] = []
396	            wrote_policy = False
397	            try:
398	                # Phase 1: every file lands carrying the shared marker.
399	                for record in records:
400	                    self.store.write_restore_pending(record, marker)
401	                    written_keys.append(record.key_id)
402	                if policy_rules is not None:
403	                    self.policy_store.write_restore_pending(
404	                        tenant_id, policy_rules, marker
405	                    )
406	                    wrote_policy = True
407	                # Phase 2: the single ledger append. The files are the outbox.
408	                # The durable append is the commit point.
409	                self.store.audit.append(event)
410	            except BaseException as exc:
411	                # Roll back every file the transaction created AND every
412	                # handle the attempt minted — including records whose file
413	                # never landed after a phase-1 failure partway through the
414	                # write set.
415	                self._rollback(
416	                    written_keys, wrote_policy, tenant_id, records
417	                )
418	                if isinstance(exc, LedgerError):
419	                    raise
420	                raise LedgerError(
421	                    "tenant restore failed before commit: %s" % exc
422	                ) from exc
423	
424	            # Phase 3: clear the markers. The commit point already passed, so
425	            # this is best-effort housekeeping: a failure here or a crash is
426	            # repaired idempotently on the next open (event is durably in the
427	            # ledger, the restored data and its handles stay authoritative).
428	            for record in records:
429	                try:
430	                    self.store.clear_restore_pending(record)
431	                except OSError:
432	                    pass
433	            if policy_rules is not None:
434	                try:
435	                    self.policy_store.clear_restore_pending(
436	                        tenant_id, policy_rules
437	                    )
438	                except OSError:
439	                    pass
440	            return RestoreResult(
441	                status=RESTORE_CREATED,
442	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
443	                key_ids=key_ids,
444	                policy_restored=policy_rules is not None,
445	            )
446	        finally:
447	            for lock_cm in reversed(locked):
448	                lock_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)
449	            if policy_taken:
450	                policy_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)
451	
452	    def _rollback(
453	        self,
454	        written_keys: List[str],
455	        wrote_policy: bool,
456	        tenant_id: str,
457	        records: Optional[list] = None,
458	    ) -> None:
459	        """Remove every file created by a restore that did not commit.
460	
461	        The provider handles the would-be records minted are deleted too —
462	        for *every* record the attempt adopted, including ones whose file
463	        never landed when phase 1 failed partway through the write set — so a
464	        failure that aborts the batch leaves no orphaned KMS/HSM objects
465	        behind.
466	        """
467	        by_id = {r.key_id: r for r in (records or [])}
468	        landed = set(written_keys)
469	        for key_id in written_keys:
470	            self.store.remove_file(key_id)
471	        for key_id, record in by_id.items():
472	            # Covers both landed (file now removed) and never-landed records.
473	            self.store.release_record_handles(record)
474	        if wrote_policy:
475	            self.policy_store.remove_restore_file(tenant_id)

477	    # -- crash recovery ----------------------------------------------------
478	    def recover(self) -> None:
479	        """Finish or roll back restores interrupted by a crash.
480	
481	        Files still carrying the shared marker are grouped by the embedded
482	        event id. When the event reached the ledger the transaction commits
483	        (markers are cleared); otherwise it never committed and every file of
484	        the group is removed. Both paths are idempotent.
485	        """
486	        groups: Dict[str, _PendingGroup] = {}
487	
488	        def group_for(marker: dict) -> _PendingGroup:
489	            eid = marker["event"]["event_id"]
490	            group = groups.get(eid)
491	            if group is None:
492	                group = _PendingGroup(marker)
493	                groups[eid] = group
494	            return group
495	
496	        data_dir = self.store.data_dir
497	        try:
498	            names = os.listdir(data_dir)
499	        except OSError:
500	            names = []
501	        for name in names:
502	            if name.startswith(_EMPTY_MARKER_PREFIX) and name.endswith(".json"):
503	                self._recover_empty_marker(os.path.join(data_dir, name))
504	                continue
505	            if not (name.endswith(".json") and _is_uuid(name[:-5])):
506	                continue

508	            record = self.store._read_record(path)

510	            if not isinstance(marker, dict) or not marker.get("_restore"):
511	                continue
512	            group_for(marker).key_files[record.key_id] = path
513

517	        except OSError:
518	            policy_names = []

523	            doc = self.policy_store._read_doc(path)

531	            group.policy_tenant = owner
532	            group.policy_rules = rules
533

549	    def _resolve_orphan_journals(self) -> None:
550	        """Reap provision journals left by restore attempts with no marker.
551	
552	        A crash after provider adoption but before the first file landed
553	        leaves a journal but no marker group; the event never committed, so
554	        every recorded handle is deleted. Marker-referenced journals are
555	        handled with their group in :meth:`recover`.
556	        """
557	        directory = os.path.join(self.store.data_dir, "provisions")
558	        try:
559	            names = os.listdir(directory)
560	        except OSError:
561	            return
562	        for name in names:
563	            if not name.endswith(".json"):
564	                continue
565	            journal_id = name[:-5]
566	            try:
567	                committed = self.store.audit.get_event(journal_id) is not None
568	            except LedgerError:
569	                continue
570	            if not committed:
571	                self.store.release_journal_handles(journal_id)
572	            self.store.drop_provision_journal(journal_id)

574	    def _recover_empty_marker(self, path: str) -> None:
575	        """Resolve an empty-restore idempotency marker after a crash.
576	
577	        A finalized marker (``event`` is null) is the persistent record that
578	        the batch committed; it stays. A marker still carrying its pending
579	        event is finished when the event reached the ledger, and removed
580	        otherwise — both idempotently, mirroring multi-file recovery.
581	        """

"""Atomic tenant restore: multi-file outbox transaction over keys and policy.

A restore writes several key files and optionally one policy document as a
single logical transaction. Every file first lands carrying the same pending
marker (the shared audit event plus a manifest of the whole write set); the
single audit event is appended to the ledger once; only then are the markers
cleared. A failure or crash at any point is repaired idempotently on the next
open, mirroring the per-key outbox in :mod:`keymgr.store` and the policy
outbox in :mod:`keymgr.policy`.

Conflict rules, applied before anything touches disk:

* a ``key_id`` that already exists for the requesting tenant is a ``409``
  (nothing is changed);
* a ``key_id`` owned by another tenant answers ``404`` so existence never
  leaks across tenants;
* a policy document already present for the tenant conflicts regardless of
  whether the bundle carries rules or an explicit null (an existing policy is
  never overwritten or deleted); a document on the tenant's hashed path that
  names another owner is treated as a foreign ``404``.

An empty bundle (``keys == []`` and ``policy is null``) creates no files but
still commits the single ``import`` event and reports success.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import threading
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Dict, Iterator, List, NamedTuple, Optional

from . import audit as audit_mod
from . import tenantbundle
from .audit import AuditEvent, LedgerError
from .policy import Rule

try:  # fcntl is POSIX-only; restores still work without cross-process locks.
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
    fcntl = None

# Restore outcomes.
RESTORE_CREATED = "created"
RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT = "same_tenant_conflict"
RESTORE_FOREIGN_CONFLICT = "foreign_conflict"

# An empty restore writes no key/policy file, so it persists its idempotency
# marker as ``restore-empty-<sha256(tenant_id)>.json`` in the data directory:
# the batch commits at most once and a repeated empty restore of the same
# tenant conflicts instead of logging a second import event.
_EMPTY_MARKER_PREFIX = "restore-empty-"


class Conflict(NamedTuple):
    """Why a restore was refused before writing anything."""

    kind: str  # "key" or "policy"
    owner: Optional[str]  # tenant that currently owns the object
    key_id: Optional[str] = None  # set for kind == "key"


class RestoreResult(NamedTuple):
    """Outcome of a restore attempt."""

    status: str
    tenant_id: Optional[str] = None
    key_ids: Optional[List[str]] = None
    policy_restored: Optional[bool] = None
    conflict: Optional[Conflict] = None


class _PendingGroup:
    """Files sharing one restore marker discovered during recovery."""

    def __init__(self, marker: dict) -> None:
        self.marker = marker
        self.key_files: Dict[str, str] = {}  # key_id -> path
        self.policy_file: Optional[str] = None
        self.policy_tenant: Optional[str] = None
        self.policy_rules: List[Rule] = []
        self.journal: Optional[str] = marker.get("journal")


class RestoreCoordinator:
    """Coordinates reads for backup and the atomic write set for restore."""

    def __init__(self, store, policy_store) -> None:
        self.store = store
        self.policy_store = policy_store
        # Serialize restores within this process; per-key fcntl locks plus the
        # policy write lock still guard individual files.
        self._restore_lock = threading.Lock()
        # Recover any multi-file transaction interrupted by a crash.
        self.recover()

    # -- backup ------------------------------------------------------------
    def backup_payload(self, tenant_id: str) -> dict:
        """Build the decrypted tenant payload {format, tenant_id, keys, policy}.

        The read runs under the tenant's policy lock and every key lock of
        the tenant (all acquired in the same sorted order the restore
        transaction uses), so the bundle is one committed view: a concurrent
        rotate/revoke/policy update in any process is either fully before or
        fully after the snapshot, never mixed into it.
        """
        key_ids = [r.key_id for r in self.store.list_for_tenant(tenant_id)]
        with self.policy_store.tenant_lock(tenant_id), self.store.multi_key_locks(
            key_ids
        ):
            # Re-read under the locks: a record listed above may have been
            # rotated or revoked since the unlocked directory scan.
            records = []
            for key_id in key_ids:
                record = self.store.read_raw(key_id)
                if record is not None and record.tenant_id == tenant_id:
                    records.append(record)
            # Lazily take over any raw pre-provider versions here, under the
            # same key locks, so the backup is one committed view. This only
            # imports/wraps while the local provider is active; with an
            # external provider active a legacy version fails 503 and the
            # backup is refused without a fallback.
            for record in records:
                self.store.prepare_backup_record(record)
            rules = self.policy_store.get(tenant_id)
            return {
                "format": tenantbundle.FORMAT,
                "tenant_id": tenant_id,
                "keys": [self.store.backup_entry(r) for r in records],
                "policy": None
                if rules is None
                else {"rules": [r.to_json() for r in rules]},
            }

    def backup_bundle(self, tenant_id: str, passphrase: str) -> str:
        """Seal the tenant's full state into an opaque backup bundle."""
        return tenantbundle.encode_bundle(
            self.backup_payload(tenant_id), passphrase
        )

    # -- restore -----------------------------------------------------------
    @contextmanager
    def _cross_process_restore_lock(self) -> Iterator[None]:
        """Serialize whole restore transactions across processes.

        The in-process ``_restore_lock`` cannot stop a second server or CLI
        process from interleaving its conflict scan with this one's writes;
        an exclusive ``fcntl`` lock on ``restore.lock`` can.
        """
        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
            yield
            return
        fd = os.open(
            os.path.join(self.store.data_dir, "restore.lock"),
            os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT,
            0o600,
        )
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            os.close(fd)

    def _empty_marker_path(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(tenant_id.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        return os.path.join(
            self.store.data_dir, _EMPTY_MARKER_PREFIX + digest + ".json"
        )

    def restore(self, tenant_id: str, payload: dict) -> RestoreResult:
        """Atomically restore a validated tenant payload.

        Returns a created result, or a conflict result after leaving every
        existing file byte-for-byte untouched. Raises LedgerError when the
        transaction cannot be committed; all written files and all handles
        minted by the attempt are rolled back.

        Ordering: every version is validated and adopted through its provider
        first (the durable provision journal records each handle as it is
        minted); only then are conflicts rechecked, files written and the
        single audit event appended. A failure, refused conflict or crash at
        any point before that commit point deletes every handle the attempt
        created; the durable event is the point of no return.
        """
        with self._restore_lock, self._cross_process_restore_lock():
            key_ids = sorted(k["key_id"] for k in payload["keys"])
            policy_rules = None
            if payload["policy"] is not None:
                policy_rules = [
                    Rule.from_json(r) for r in payload["policy"]["rules"]
                ]

            # Mint the committing event up front so the provision journal is
            # named after its event_id, letting startup recovery decide
            # committed-vs-not purely from the ledger.
            event = self.store.audit.new_event(
                tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT, None,
                audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
            )
            journal_id, journal_path = self.store._new_provision_journal(
                event.event_id
            )
            try:
                # Phase 0: complete ALL version validation and provider
                # calls before the conflict recheck or any file write.
                records = []
                try:
                    for key_id in key_ids:
                        entry = next(
                            k for k in payload["keys"] if k["key_id"] == key_id
                        )
                        records.append(
                            self.store.record_from_backup(
                                tenant_id, entry, journal_path
                            )
                        )
                except BaseException:
                    # A later key/version failed: release the handles the
                    # earlier records already minted (record_from_backup
                    # released its own record's handles; do the rest here).
                    for record in records:
                        self.store.release_record_handles(record)
                    raise

                # Conflict scan only after every provider call succeeded.
                # Any foreign owner anywhere wins (404); otherwise a
                # same-tenant owner is a 409. Repeated under every lock.
                conflict = self._scan_conflicts(tenant_id, key_ids)
                if conflict is not None:
                    # Nothing was written; release every minted handle.
                    for record in records:
                        self.store.release_record_handles(record)
                    status = (
                        RESTORE_FOREIGN_CONFLICT
                        if conflict.owner != tenant_id
                        else RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT
                    )
                    return RestoreResult(status=status, conflict=conflict)

                writes_policy = policy_rules is not None

                if not key_ids and not writes_policy:
                    # Empty bundle: no key/policy files or handles, but the
                    # batch still commits a persistent idempotency marker plus
                    # its single import event.
                    with self.policy_store.tenant_lock(tenant_id):
                        policy_path = self.policy_store.path_for(tenant_id)
                        if os.path.exists(policy_path):
                            owner = self.policy_store.owner_of_path(policy_path)
                            if owner is not None and owner != tenant_id:
                                return RestoreResult(
                                    status=RESTORE_FOREIGN_CONFLICT,
                                    conflict=Conflict(kind="policy", owner=owner),
                                )
                            return RestoreResult(
                                status=RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT,
                                conflict=Conflict(kind="policy", owner=tenant_id),
                            )
                        return self._commit_empty(tenant_id, event)

                marker = {
                    "_restore": True,
                    "event": event.to_json(),
                    "tenant_id": tenant_id,
                    "key_ids": key_ids,
                    "policy": writes_policy,
                    # Ties the marker group to the attempt's handle journal.
                    "journal": journal_id,
                }

                return self._commit(
                    tenant_id, key_ids, records, policy_rules, event, marker
                )
            finally:
                # On a normal return (success, refused conflict or a handled
                # rollback) the handles were either committed to the records
                # or released; the journal is spent. A hard crash leaves it on
                # disk for startup recovery, which is the actual safety net.
                self.store.drop_provision_journal(journal_id)

    def _commit_empty(self, tenant_id: str, event: AuditEvent) -> RestoreResult:
        """Commit an empty restore: idempotency marker + one import event.

        The marker file first lands carrying the pending event, the event is
        appended, then the marker is finalized with the event cleared. A
        ledger failure removes the marker (nothing commits); a crash is
        repaired by recovery exactly like a multi-file restore group.
        """
        path = self._empty_marker_path(tenant_id)
        if os.path.exists(path):
            # This tenant already committed an empty restore batch.
            return RestoreResult(
                status=RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT,
                conflict=Conflict(kind="batch", owner=tenant_id),
            )
        marker = {
            "_restore": True,
            "_empty": True,
            "event": event.to_json(),
            "tenant_id": tenant_id,
            "key_ids": [],
            "policy": False,
        }
        self.store._write_atomic(path, marker)
        try:
            self.store.audit.append(event)
        except BaseException:
            try:
                os.unlink(path)
            except OSError:
                pass
            raise
        finalized = dict(marker)
        finalized["event"] = None
        self.store._write_atomic(path, finalized)
        return RestoreResult(
            status=RESTORE_CREATED,
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            key_ids=[],
            policy_restored=False,
        )

    def _scan_conflicts(
        self, tenant_id: str, key_ids: List[str]
    ) -> Optional[Conflict]:
        """Return the first conflict (foreign owners take priority).

        A policy document already present for the tenant conflicts even when
        the bundle's policy slot is null: a restore never overwrites or
        deletes an existing policy.
        """
        same_tenant: Optional[Conflict] = None
        for key_id in key_ids:
            existing = self.store.read_raw(key_id)
            if existing is None:
                continue
            if existing.tenant_id != tenant_id:
                # A foreign key answers 404 immediately and suppresses any
                # same-tenant 409, so cross-tenant existence never leaks.
                return Conflict(
                    kind="key", owner=existing.tenant_id, key_id=key_id
                )
            if same_tenant is None:
                same_tenant = Conflict(
                    kind="key", owner=tenant_id, key_id=key_id
                )
        path = self.policy_store.path_for(tenant_id)
        if os.path.exists(path):
            owner = self.policy_store.owner_of_path(path)
            if owner is not None and owner != tenant_id:
                # The tenant's hashed path holds a document naming another
                # tenant; treat it like a foreign occupation.
                return Conflict(kind="policy", owner=owner)
            if same_tenant is None:
                same_tenant = Conflict(kind="policy", owner=tenant_id)
        return same_tenant

    def _commit(
        self,
        tenant_id: str,
        key_ids: List[str],
        records: list,
        policy_rules: Optional[List[Rule]],
        event: AuditEvent,
        marker: dict,
    ) -> RestoreResult:
        """Run the multi-file outbox transaction under all required locks."""
        locked = []
        policy_cm = self.policy_store.tenant_lock(tenant_id)
        policy_taken = False
        try:
            policy_cm.__enter__()
            policy_taken = True
            for key_id in key_ids:
                lock_cm = self.store.key_locks(key_id)
                lock_cm.__enter__()
                locked.append(lock_cm)

            # Re-scan now that every file lock is held.
            conflict = self._scan_conflicts(tenant_id, key_ids)
            if conflict is not None:
                status = (
                    RESTORE_FOREIGN_CONFLICT
                    if conflict.owner != tenant_id
                    else RESTORE_SAME_TENANT_CONFLICT
                )
                # The provider objects were minted before the locks, but no
                # file now commits: release the handles so the backend leaks
                # nothing on the lost conflict race.
                for record in records:
                    self.store.release_record_handles(record)
                return RestoreResult(status=status, conflict=conflict)

            written_keys: List[str] = []
            wrote_policy = False
            try:
                # Phase 1: every file lands carrying the shared marker.
                for record in records:
                    self.store.write_restore_pending(record, marker)
                    written_keys.append(record.key_id)
                if policy_rules is not None:
                    self.policy_store.write_restore_pending(
                        tenant_id, policy_rules, marker
                    )
                    wrote_policy = True
                # Phase 2: the single ledger append. The files are the outbox.
                # The durable append is the commit point.
                self.store.audit.append(event)
            except BaseException as exc:
                # Roll back every file the transaction created AND every
                # handle the attempt minted — including records whose file
                # never landed after a phase-1 failure partway through the
                # write set.
                self._rollback(
                    written_keys, wrote_policy, tenant_id, records
                )
                if isinstance(exc, LedgerError):
                    raise
                raise LedgerError(
                    "tenant restore failed before commit: %s" % exc
                ) from exc

            # Phase 3: clear the markers. The commit point already passed, so
            # this is best-effort housekeeping: a failure here or a crash is
            # repaired idempotently on the next open (event is durably in the
            # ledger, the restored data and its handles stay authoritative).
            for record in records:
                try:
                    self.store.clear_restore_pending(record)
                except OSError:
                    pass
            if policy_rules is not None:
                try:
                    self.policy_store.clear_restore_pending(
                        tenant_id, policy_rules
                    )
                except OSError:
                    pass
            return RestoreResult(
                status=RESTORE_CREATED,
                tenant_id=tenant_id,
                key_ids=key_ids,
                policy_restored=policy_rules is not None,
            )
        finally:
            for lock_cm in reversed(locked):
                lock_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)
            if policy_taken:
                policy_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)

    def _rollback(
        self,
        written_keys: List[str],
        wrote_policy: bool,
        tenant_id: str,
        records: Optional[list] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Remove every file created by a restore that did not commit.

        The provider handles the would-be records minted are deleted too —
        for *every* record the attempt adopted, including ones whose file
        never landed when phase 1 failed partway through the write set — so a
        failure that aborts the batch leaves no orphaned KMS/HSM objects
        behind.
        """
        by_id = {r.key_id: r for r in (records or [])}
        landed = set(written_keys)
        for key_id in written_keys:
            self.store.remove_file(key_id)
        for key_id, record in by_id.items():
            # Covers both landed (file now removed) and never-landed records.
            self.store.release_record_handles(record)
        if wrote_policy:
            self.policy_store.remove_restore_file(tenant_id)

    # -- crash recovery ----------------------------------------------------
    def recover(self) -> None:
        """Finish or roll back restores interrupted by a crash.

        Files still carrying the shared marker are grouped by the embedded
        event id. When the event reached the ledger the transaction commits
        (markers are cleared); otherwise it never committed and every file of
        the group is removed. Both paths are idempotent.
        """
        groups: Dict[str, _PendingGroup] = {}

        def group_for(marker: dict) -> _PendingGroup:
            eid = marker["event"]["event_id"]
            group = groups.get(eid)
            if group is None:
                group = _PendingGroup(marker)
                groups[eid] = group
            return group

        data_dir = self.store.data_dir
        try:
            names = os.listdir(data_dir)
        except OSError:
            names = []
        for name in names:
            if name.startswith(_EMPTY_MARKER_PREFIX) and name.endswith(".json"):
                self._recover_empty_marker(os.path.join(data_dir, name))
                continue
            if not (name.endswith(".json") and _is_uuid(name[:-5])):
                continue
            path = os.path.join(data_dir, name)
            record = self.store._read_record(path)
            marker = getattr(record, "pending_event", None)
            if not isinstance(marker, dict) or not marker.get("_restore"):
                continue
            group_for(marker).key_files[record.key_id] = path

        policy_dir = self.policy_store.dir_path
        try:
            policy_names = os.listdir(policy_dir)
        except OSError:
            policy_names = []
        for name in policy_names:
            if not name.endswith(".json"):
                continue
            path = os.path.join(policy_dir, name)
            doc = self.policy_store._read_doc(path)
            if doc is None:
                continue
            owner, rules, pending = doc
            if not isinstance(pending, dict) or not pending.get("_restore"):
                continue
            group = group_for(pending)
            group.policy_file = path
            group.policy_tenant = owner
            group.policy_rules = rules

        for eid, group in groups.items():
            if not self._recover_group(eid, group):
                # The ledger could not be read; leave files and journal for a
                # later open to retry rather than risking committed material.
                continue
            # The group is resolved (committed or rolled back); its handle
            # journal, deferred from the store's own startup sweep, is now
            # spent. On the uncommitted path _recover_group already deleted
            # every handle the journal recorded.
            self.store.drop_provision_journal(group.journal)

        # Journals with no marker group (crash before the first file landed)
        # are swept last; their event never committed.
        self._resolve_orphan_journals()

    def _resolve_orphan_journals(self) -> None:
        """Reap provision journals left by restore attempts with no marker.

        A crash after provider adoption but before the first file landed
        leaves a journal but no marker group; the event never committed, so
        every recorded handle is deleted. Marker-referenced journals are
        handled with their group in :meth:`recover`.
        """
        directory = os.path.join(self.store.data_dir, "provisions")
        try:
            names = os.listdir(directory)
        except OSError:
            return
        for name in names:
            if not name.endswith(".json"):
                continue
            journal_id = name[:-5]
            try:
                committed = self.store.audit.get_event(journal_id) is not None
            except LedgerError:
                continue
            if not committed:
                self.store.release_journal_handles(journal_id)
            self.store.drop_provision_journal(journal_id)

    def _recover_empty_marker(self, path: str) -> None:
        """Resolve an empty-restore idempotency marker after a crash.

        A finalized marker (``event`` is null) is the persistent record that
        the batch committed; it stays. A marker still carrying its pending
        event is finished when the event reached the ledger, and removed
        otherwise — both idempotently, mirroring multi-file recovery.
        """
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                marker = json.load(fh)
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            return
        if not isinstance(marker, dict) or not marker.get("_restore"):
            return
        event = marker.get("event")
        if not event:
            return  # finalized marker: the committed batch's idempotency record
        try:
            committed = self.store.audit.get_event(event["event_id"]) is not None
        except (LedgerError, KeyError, TypeError):
            return  # leave it for a later open to retry
        if committed:
            finalized = dict(marker)
            finalized["event"] = None
            self.store._write_atomic(path, finalized)
        else:
            try:
                os.unlink(path)
            except OSError:
                pass

    def _recover_group(self, eid: str, group: _PendingGroup) -> bool:
        """Resolve one marker group. True if resolved, False to retry later."""
        marker = group.marker
        tenant_id = marker["tenant_id"]
        try:
            committed = self.store.audit.get_event(eid) is not None
        except LedgerError:
            # Leave the group untouched; a later open retries recovery.
            return False
        if not committed:
            # The ledger append never happened: remove every partial file and
            # release every provider handle the batch minted (the journal
            # also covers records whose file never landed), so a crash before
            # commit leaves no orphaned KMS/HSM objects.
            if group.journal:
                self.store.release_journal_handles(group.journal)
            for key_id, path in list(group.key_files.items()):
                record = self.store._read_record(path)
                if record is not None and not group.journal:
                    # No journal available: fall back to the handles carried
                    # by the landed files themselves.
                    self.store.release_record_handles(record)
                self.store.remove_file(key_id)
            if group.policy_file is not None:
                self.policy_store.remove_restore_file(tenant_id)
            return True
        # Committed: finish the transaction by clearing the markers. This is
        # post-commit housekeeping and best-effort; a rewrite failure leaves
        # the marker for the next open and never rolls the data back.
        for key_id, path in group.key_files.items():
            record = self.store._read_record(path)
            if record is None or not record.pending_event:
                continue
            try:
                self.store.clear_restore_pending(record)
            except OSError:
                pass
        if group.policy_file is not None:
            try:
                self.policy_store.clear_restore_pending(
                    group.policy_tenant or tenant_id, group.policy_rules
                )
            except OSError:
                pass
        return True


def _is_uuid(value: str) -> bool:
    from .store import is_valid_key_id

    return is_valid_key_id(value)

1	"""Per-tenant action policies: validation, persistence and enforcement.
2	
3	A policy document is a list of rules; each rule binds a ``subject`` (the
4	X-Operator-Id of the caller), a set of ``actions`` and an ``effect`` of
5	``allow`` or ``deny``. Enforcement, for one (tenant, subject, action):
6	
7	* a tenant with no document is unrestricted (every action is allowed);
8	* among the rules whose subject equals the caller and whose actions contain
9	  the action, any ``deny`` wins over ``allow``;
10	* if no matching rule exists the action is denied (default deny).
11	
12	Documents are stored as one JSON file per tenant, written through the same
13	outbox transaction as key records: the file first lands carrying the audit
14	event, the ledger append follows, then the marker is cleared; a crash in
15	between is repaired idempotently on the next open.
16	"""
17	
18	import hashlib
19	import json
20	import os
21	import tempfile
22	import threading
23	from contextlib import contextmanager
24	from dataclasses import dataclass
25	from typing import Iterator, List, Optional
26	
27	from . import audit as audit_mod
28	from .audit import AuditEvent, AuditLog, LedgerError
29	
30	try:  # fcntl is POSIX-only; policy writes still work without it.
31	    import fcntl
32	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
33	    fcntl = None
34	
35	# Actions a policy rule can govern. These are the same action names the audit
36	# ledger uses (the management actions policy_* are deliberately not governable).
37	POLICY_ACTIONS = (
38	    "create",
39	    "read",
40	    "rotate",
41	    "revoke",
42	    "import",
43	    "export",
44	    "audit",
45	)
46	EFFECTS = ("allow", "deny")
47	_POLICY_DIR = "policies"
48	
49	
50	class PolicyError(ValueError):
51	    """A policy document or rule failed validation (surfaced as 400)."""
52	
53	
54	@dataclass(frozen=True)
55	class Rule:
56	    """One policy rule: an effect on a set of actions for one subject."""
57	
58	    subject: str
59	    actions: List[str]
60	    effect: str
61	
62	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
63	        """Serialize to a plain dict; actions are emitted sorted."""
64	        return {
65	            "subject": self.subject,
66	            "actions": list(self.actions),
67	            "effect": self.effect,
68	        }
69	
70	    @classmethod
71	    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "Rule":
72	        # Documents on disk were validated when written, but validate again
73	        # on the way in so a hand-edited file can never break enforcement.
74	        return validate_rule(data)
75	
76	    def signature(self):
77	        """Dedup key: same subject/effect with the same unordered action set."""
78	        return self.subject, self.effect, frozenset(self.actions)
79	
80	
81	def validate_rule(raw, index: Optional[int] = None) -> Rule:
82	    """Validate one rule object; raise PolicyError naming the bad field.
83	
84	    ``index`` prefixes field names with ``rules[i].`` when the rule comes from
85	    a document; a standalone rule names the bare fields.
86	    """
87	    where = "rules[%d]." % index if index is not None else ""
88	
89	    def err(message: str) -> PolicyError:
90	        return PolicyError(message)
91	
92	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
93	        raise err("field %s must be an object" % (where.rstrip(".") if index is not None else "rule"))
94	    known = {"subject", "actions", "effect"}
95	    unknown = set(raw) - known
96	    if unknown:
97	        raise err(
98	            "unknown field %s%s"
99	            % (where, sorted(unknown)[0])
100	        )
101	    subject = raw.get("subject")
102	    if not isinstance(subject, str) or not subject:
103	        raise err("field %ssubject must be a non-empty string" % where)
104	    effect = raw.get("effect")
105	    if not isinstance(effect, str) or effect not in EFFECTS:
106	        raise err(
107	            "field %seffect must be one of: %s"
108	            % (where, ", ".join(EFFECTS))
109	        )
110	    actions = raw.get("actions")
111	    if not isinstance(actions, list) or not actions:
112	        raise err(
113	            "field %sactions must be a non-empty array" % where
114	        )
115	    clean_actions = []
116	    for action in actions:
117	        if not isinstance(action, str) or not action:
118	            raise err(
119	                "field %sactions must be non-empty strings" % where
120	            )
121	        if action not in POLICY_ACTIONS:
122	            raise err(
123	                "field %sactions has unknown action %r (allowed: %s)"
124	                % (where, action, ", ".join(POLICY_ACTIONS))
125	            )
126	        if action not in clean_actions:
127	            # Duplicates within one rule are dropped, not an error: the action
128	            # set is unordered, so ["read", "read"] carries no extra meaning.
129	            clean_actions.append(action)
130	    return Rule(subject=subject, actions=clean_actions, effect=effect)
131	
132	
133	def validate_rules(raw) -> List[Rule]:
134	    """Validate a full rules array; [] is valid and means default-deny."""
135	    if not isinstance(raw, list):
136	        raise PolicyError("field rules must be an array")
137	    rules: List[Rule] = []
138	    seen = set()
139	    for index, item in enumerate(raw):
140	        rule = validate_rule(item, index)
141	        if rule.signature() in seen:
142	            raise PolicyError(
143	                "field rules contains a duplicate rule at index %d "
144	                "(same subject, effect and unordered actions)" % index
145	            )
146	        seen.add(rule.signature())
147	        rules.append(rule)
148	    return rules
149	
150	
151	class PolicyStore:
152	    """File-backed per-tenant policy documents."""
153	
154	    def __init__(self, data_dir: str, audit_log: Optional[AuditLog] = None) -> None:
155	        self.data_dir = data_dir
156	        self.dir_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _POLICY_DIR)
157	        os.makedirs(self.dir_path, exist_ok=True)
158	        self.audit = audit_log if audit_log is not None else AuditLog(data_dir)
159	        self._write_lock = threading.Lock()
160	        self._recover_pending_events()
161	
162	    # -- on-disk shape -----------------------------------------------------
163	    def path_for(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
164	        """Public accessor for a tenant's policy document path."""
165	        return self._path_for(tenant_id)
166	
167	    def _path_for(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
168	        # Tenant ids are free-form strings, so never use them as a filename:
169	        # key the file by a digest of the tenant instead.
170	        digest = hashlib.sha256(tenant_id.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
171	        return os.path.join(self.dir_path, digest + ".json")
172	
173	    def _lock_path_for(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
174	        digest = hashlib.sha256(tenant_id.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
175	        return os.path.join(self.dir_path, digest + ".lock")
176	
177	    @contextmanager
178	    def tenant_lock(self, tenant_id: str) -> Iterator[None]:
179	        """Serialize all writes to one tenant's policy across processes.
180	
181	        Pairs the in-process write lock with an exclusive ``fcntl`` lock on a
182	        per-tenant sidecar file, so a put/delete/restore/backup in another
183	        process cannot interleave with this one's read-modify-write.
184	        """
185	        with self._write_lock:
186	            if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
187	                yield
188	                return
189	            fd = os.open(
190	                self._lock_path_for(tenant_id), os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600
191	            )
192	            try:
193	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
194	                yield
195	            finally:
196	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
197	                os.close(fd)
198	
199	    def _write_atomic(self, path: str, payload: dict) -> None:
200	        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=self.dir_path, suffix=".tmp")
201	        try:
202	            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
203	                json.dump(payload, fh)
204	                fh.flush()
205	                os.fsync(fh.fileno())
206	            os.chmod(tmp_path, 0o600)
207	            os.replace(tmp_path, path)
208	        except BaseException:
209	            try:
210	                os.unlink(tmp_path)
211	            except OSError:
212	                pass
213	            raise
214	
215	    def _read_doc(self, path: str):
216	        """Return (tenant_id, rules, pending_event), or None if unreadable."""
217	        try:
218	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
219	                data = json.load(fh)
220	        except (OSError, ValueError):
221	            return None
222	        try:
223	            rules = [Rule.from_json(r) for r in data["rules"]]
224	            return data["tenant_id"], rules, data.get("pending_event")
225	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, PolicyError):
226	            return None
227	
228	    def _recover_pending_events(self) -> None:
229	        """Commit outbox events left pending by a crashed process."""
230	        try:
231	            names = os.listdir(self.dir_path)
232	        except OSError:
233	            return
234	        for name in names:
235	            if not name.endswith(".json") and not name.endswith(".json.del"):
236	                continue
237	            path = os.path.join(self.dir_path, name)
238	            doc = self._read_doc(path)
239	            if doc is None:
240	                continue
241	            tenant_id, rules, pending_event = doc
242	            if not pending_event:
243	                # A tombstone left behind after a successful ledger append:
244	                # finish the delete.
245	                if name.endswith(".del"):
246	                    try:
247	                        os.unlink(path)
248	                    except OSError:
249	                        pass
250	                continue
251	            # A multi-file tenant restore transaction is resolved by the
252	            # RestoreCoordinator (its manifest drives the shared event).
253	            if isinstance(pending_event, dict) and pending_event.get("_restore"):
254	                continue
255	            event = AuditEvent.from_json(pending_event)
256	            if name.endswith(".json.del"):                # A delete tombstone. If the original file is still on disk the
257	                # crash happened before the unlink, so the delete never
258	                # happened: discard the tombstone without appending. Otherwise
259	                # finish the transaction (append is idempotent on event_id).
260	                original = path[: -len(".del")]
261	                if os.path.exists(original):
262	                    try:
263	                        os.unlink(path)
264	                    except OSError:
265	                        pass
266	                    continue
267	                self.audit.append(event)
268	                try:
269	                    os.unlink(path)
270	                except OSError:
271	                    pass
272	            else:
273	                # append() is idempotent on event_id.
274	                self.audit.append(event)
275	                self._write_atomic(
276	                    path,
277	                    {"tenant_id": tenant_id,
278	                     "rules": [r.to_json() for r in rules],
279	                     "pending_event": None},
280	                )
281	
282	    def _commit_put(self, tenant_id: str, rules: List[Rule],
283	                    event: AuditEvent, existed: bool, previous: Optional[dict]):
284	        """Write a document and its event as one logical transaction."""
285	        path = self._path_for(tenant_id)
286	        doc = {
287	            "tenant_id": tenant_id,
288	            "rules": [r.to_json() for r in rules],
289	            "pending_event": event.to_json(),
290	        }
291	        self._write_atomic(path, doc)
292	        try:
293	            self.audit.append(event)
294	        except BaseException:
295	            if not existed:
296	                try:
297	                    os.unlink(path)
298	                except OSError:
299	                    pass
300	            elif previous is not None:
301	                self._write_atomic(path, previous)
302	            raise
303	        # The durable ledger append is the commit point; clearing the marker
304	        # is post-commit housekeeping. A failure here leaves the marker for
305	        # startup recovery and must never roll the document back or fail the
306	        # request.
307	        doc["pending_event"] = None
308	        try:
309	            self._write_atomic(path, doc)
310	        except OSError:
311	            pass
312	
313	    # -- public API --------------------------------------------------------
314	    def get(self, tenant_id: str) -> Optional[List[Rule]]:
315	        """Return the tenant's rules, or None when no document exists."""
316	        doc = self._read_doc(self._path_for(tenant_id))
317	        if doc is None:
318	            return None
319	        return doc[1]
320	
321	    def put(self, tenant_id: str, rules: List[Rule]) -> List[Rule]:
322	        """Replace (or create) the tenant's document and audit policy_update."""
323	        with self.tenant_lock(tenant_id):
324	            path = self._path_for(tenant_id)
325	            existed = os.path.exists(path)
326	            previous = None
327	            if existed:
328	                try:
329	                    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
330	                        previous = json.load(fh)
331	                except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
332	                    raise LedgerError(
333	                        "cannot read policy document: %s" % exc
334	                    ) from exc
335	            event = self.audit.new_event(
336	                tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_POLICY_UPDATE, None,
337	                audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
338	            )
339	            self._commit_put(tenant_id, rules, event, existed, previous)
340	        return rules
341	
342	    def delete(self, tenant_id: str) -> None:
343	        """Delete the tenant's document and audit policy_delete.
344	
345	        Tombstone sequence: write a ``.json.del`` marker carrying the event,
346	        unlink the document, append the event, then remove the marker. A crash
347	        between any two steps is repaired on the next open. If the ledger
348	        append itself fails, the original document is restored byte-for-byte
349	        and the tombstone discarded, so a failed delete never takes effect.
350	        Deleting a tenant that has no document still records the event.
351	        """
352	        with self.tenant_lock(tenant_id):
353	            path = self._path_for(tenant_id)
354	            existed = os.path.exists(path)
355	            event = self.audit.new_event(
356	                tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_POLICY_DELETE, None,
357	                audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
358	            )
359	            if not existed:
360	                self.audit.append(event)
361	                return
362	            try:
363	                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
364	                    previous = json.load(fh)
365	            except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
366	                raise LedgerError(
367	                    "cannot read policy document: %s" % exc
368	                ) from exc
369	            tombstone = path + ".del"
370	            self._write_atomic(
371	                tombstone,
372	                {"tenant_id": tenant_id, "rules": [],
373	                 "pending_event": event.to_json()},
374	            )
375	            os.unlink(path)
376	            try:
377	                # From here on a crash is repaired from the tombstone; the
378	                # append is idempotent on event_id.
379	                self.audit.append(event)
380	            except BaseException:
381	                # The ledger write failed: roll the delete back so the
382	                # document and its event never diverge.
383	                self._write_atomic(path, previous)
384	                try:
385	                    os.unlink(tombstone)
386	                except OSError:
387	                    pass
388	                raise
389	            try:
390	                os.unlink(tombstone)
391	            except OSError:
392	                pass
393	
394	    def audit_read(self, tenant_id: str) -> None:
395	        """Record a successful policy_read (the document is never modified)."""
396	        event = self.audit.new_event(
397	            tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_POLICY_READ, None,
398	            audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
399	        )
400	        self.audit.append(event)
401	
402	    def is_allowed(self, tenant_id: str, action: str, subject: str) -> bool:
403	        """Enforce the tenant document for (subject, action).
404	
405	        No document means unrestricted. Otherwise deny wins, and an action no
406	        rule matches is denied.
407	        """
408	        rules = self.get(tenant_id)
409	        if rules is None:
410	            return True
411	        allowed = False
412	        for rule in rules:
413	            if rule.subject != subject or action not in rule.actions:
414	                continue
415	            if rule.effect == "deny":
416	                return False
417	            allowed = True
418	        return allowed
419	
420	    # -- tenant restore hooks ---------------------------------------------
421	    def owner_of_path(self, path: str) -> Optional[str]:
422	        """Return the owning tenant_id recorded inside a policy file."""

1	"""KMS/HSM provider abstraction.
2	
3	Every private key is owned by a *provider*: a local software key store by
4	default, or an external KMS/HSM reached through the ``module:factory`` entry
5	point named by ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER``. The rest of the package never touches raw
6	key material when a provider is in use: it only persists the opaque
7	``provider_id`` / ``handle`` / ``encrypted_material`` triple a provider
8	returns, and asks the provider to turn a handle back into exportable material.
9	
10	Provider contract
11	-----------------
12	A provider instance exposes:
13	
14	* ``provider_id``: a non-empty string;
15	* ``capabilities``: ``{"algorithms": ["AES256", "RSA2048"],
16	  "operations": ["generate", "rotate", "import_material",
17	  "export_material", "delete"]}``;
18	* ``generate(algorithm)`` / ``rotate(algorithm)`` ->
19	  ``{"handle", "public_key", "encrypted_material"}``;
20	* ``import_material(algorithm, public_key, material)`` -> the same triple;
21	* ``export_material(handle)`` -> ``{"public_key", "encrypted_material"}``;
22	* ``delete(handle)`` -> ``None``, idempotent.
23	
24	The factory named by ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER=module:factory`` is imported lazily on
25	first use and called with no arguments. A missing module/factory, a factory
26	raising, or a returned object failing the contract all raise
27	:class:`ProviderUnavailable`; the service answers ``503`` (CLI exit ``1``) and
28	never falls back to the local provider.
29	"""
30	
31	import base64
32	import importlib
33	import json
34	import os
35	import tempfile
36	import threading
37	import uuid
38	from typing import NamedTuple, Optional
39	
40	from cryptography.exceptions import UnsupportedAlgorithm
41	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
42	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
43	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
44	
45	from .crypto import SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS, generate_key
46	
47	#: Default provider id and the id of the built-in software provider.
48	LOCAL_PROVIDER_ID = "local"
49	
50	OP_GENERATE = "generate"
51	OP_ROTATE = "rotate"
52	OP_IMPORT_MATERIAL = "import_material"
53	OP_EXPORT_MATERIAL = "export_material"
54	OP_DELETE = "delete"
55	OPERATIONS = (
56	    OP_GENERATE,
57	    OP_ROTATE,
58	    OP_IMPORT_MATERIAL,
59	    OP_EXPORT_MATERIAL,
60	    OP_DELETE,
61	)
62	
63	_DEK_NAME = "local.dek"
64	_REGISTRY_NAME = "local-registry.json"
65	# Prefix for material wrapped by the local DEK; never reused for another
66	# encoding so wrapped blobs are self-describing on disk.
67	_WRAP_PREFIX = "pev1."
68	_NONCE_LEN = 12

71	class ProviderError(Exception):
72	    """Base class for provider failures."""
73	
74	
75	class ProviderUnavailable(ProviderError):
76	    """The provider cannot service the request (load/backend/handle failure).
77	
78	    Surfaced as HTTP ``503`` / CLI exit code ``1``. The message is logged
79	    server-side; clients only ever see a generic status (handles and material
80	    never leave the boundary).
81	    """
82	
83	
84	class ProviderInvalidMaterial(ProviderError):
85	    """Material handed to the provider is malformed for the algorithm.
86	
87	    Surfaced as HTTP ``400`` / CLI exit code ``2``; the message names the
88	    offending field but never embeds the material itself.
89	    """
90	
91	
92	class MaterialTriple(NamedTuple):
93	    """The provider-owned result of generate/rotate/import_material."""
94	
95	    handle: str
96	    public_key: Optional[str]
97	    encrypted_material: str
98	
99	
100	class ExportedMaterial(NamedTuple):
101	    """Result of export_material: material plus its public component."""
102	
103	    public_key: Optional[str]
104	    encrypted_material: str
